title: After 3 days in detention, ASEAN protesters ordered released
summary: Prosecutors dismissed complaints of malicious mischief and alarms and scandals for lack of evidence.

blocks.text: Protesters march during a demonstration that coincides with the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Leaders' Summit and Related Summits in Manila on November 15, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — After three days in detention, more than 200 protesters arrested during an ASEAN-related rally in Muntinlupa City were ordered released on Wednesday, although they still face preliminary investigation over several complaints.
In a resolution dated November 18, the Muntinlupa City Prosecutor's Office dismissed complaints of malicious mischief and alarms and scandals against the protesters for lack of prima facie evidence.
Senior Assistant City Prosecutor Elvin Keith Barrios, however, referred the remaining complaints for further preliminary investigation.

These include alleged violations of Batas Pambansa 880, or the Public Assembly Act, and provisions of the Revised Penal Code on resistance and disobedience to a person in authority and grave coercion.
Barrios also denied a motion filed by the National Union of Peoples' Lawyers seeking the dismissal of all complaints against the protesters.

"The remaining charges were referred for further preliminary investigation where the respondents may submit counter-affidavits and evidence in support of their defenses," Department of Justice spokesperson Polo Martinez said.
In a message to reporters Wednesday evening, Martinez said the police had referred 233 individuals to the Muntinlupa City Prosecutor's Office, including 213 adults and 20 minors.
Citing the prosecutor's office, Martinez confirmed that all 20 minors had been released.
Prosecutors also dismissed the complaints against six children below the age of 15, who were released to the custody of their parents or legal guardians for appropriate intervention.

"OCP Muntinlupa also ordered the release of all other respondents pending the conduct of preliminary investigation as to the remaining charges. In view of that order, it deemed the request by respondents for immediate release moot," Martinez said.
More than 200 protesters were arrested in separate demonstrations across Metro Manila on Sunday, November 15, as regional leaders gathered for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit.

The arrests drew condemnation from human rights organizations, lawmakers and members of the clergy, with several groups calling for the protesters' immediate release and investigations into alleged police abuses.
